chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ibn Faddal from 'Ali ibn 'Uqbah and a number of our companions from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon them) said:

"There is no khums in less than twenty mithqals of gold. When it reaches twenty mithqals, one-half mithqal is due until it reaches twenty-four. When it reaches twenty-four, three-fifths of a dinar is due until it reaches twenty-eight. On this calculation, for every four [mithqals] added, [the amount due] increases."

key_terms.مِثْقَالاً: mithqal (a unit of weight for gold)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of gold subject to khums and how is it calculated?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the nisab and progressive rates for Zakat on gold, establishing a minimum threshold of twenty mithqals before liability begins. It outlines a specific graduated scale where the Zakat amount increases by three-fifths of a dinar for every additional four mithqals, reflecting the precise jurisprudential calculations of the Imams. This progressive structure highlights the Shia emphasis on equitable distribution based on wealth accumulation rather than a flat rate.
